exam.subject: General Science
exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2024 General Science (4076)

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles is found in all prokaryotic cells but only in some eukaryotic cells?
explanation_steps: All prokaryotes (like bacteria) possess a cell wall. Among eukaryotes, cell walls are found in plants, fungi, and some protists, but are completely absent in animal cells. Options B and D are in all cells, while C and E are only in eukaryotes.

questions.stem: In an ecosystem, the energy flow is
explanation_steps: Energy enters an ecosystem from the sun and is captured by producers. It then moves to consumers and decomposers. Unlike nutrients, energy cannot be recycled back to the sun; it is lost as heat. Therefore, it flows in only one direction.

questions.stem: All of the following are plants, except
explanation_steps: Herbs, shrubs, ferns, and weeds belong to the Kingdom Plantae. Molds, however, are a type of fungus and belong to the Kingdom Fungi.

questions.stem: All are true about human body glands (both endocrine and exocrine), except

options.D: exocrine glands include sweat and salivary glands.

explanation_steps: All the statements A, B, C, and D are factually correct descriptions of exocrine and endocrine glands. Since there is no incorrect statement, 'None of the above' is selected.

questions.stem: Cyanobacteria reproduce by
explanation_steps: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic organisms. Like most bacteria, they primarily reproduce asexually through binary fission, where one cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

questions.stem: Saturated fats

options.B: have double bonds within the carbon chain.
options.C: tend to dissolve in water easily.

explanation_steps: Saturated fats are typically solids at room temperature, have only single bonds in their carbon chains, are insoluble in water, and are mostly animal fats. Since A, B, C, and D describe unsaturated fats or are false, E is the correct answer.

questions.stem: The largest endocrine and exocrine human body glands, respectively, are
explanation_steps: The thyroid is the largest purely endocrine gland. The liver is the largest exocrine gland (and the largest internal organ overall).

questions.stem: The Appendicular skeleton is comprised of ________ bones.
explanation_steps: The human skeleton (206 bones total) is divided into the Axial skeleton (80 bones - skull, ribs, spine) and the Appendicular skeleton (126 bones - limbs and girdles).

questions.stem: Changes in an organism that take place over time describe the process of
explanation_steps: Development refers to the structured series of changes an organism undergoes from its initial stage through to maturity. Growth specifically refers to the increase in physical size/mass.

questions.stem: The monomers that make up polypeptides and DNA, respectively, are
explanation_steps: Polypeptides (proteins) are polymers made of amino acid monomers. DNA is a polymer made of nucleotide monomers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to distinguish between species?
explanation_steps: According to the Biological Species Concept, the primary factor that distinguishes one species from another is reproductive isolation (reproductive barriers). This prevents different species from interbreeding and producing fertile offspring.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **incorrectly** paired?

options.A: Hinge joint → between humerus and pectoral girdle
options.B: Pivot joint → between atlas and axis
options.D: More than one of the above

explanation_steps: The joint between the humerus and the pectoral girdle (shoulder) is a ball-and-socket joint, not a hinge joint. Hinge joints are found in the elbow and knee.

questions.stem: The needle-like leaves of coniferous trees prevent them from
explanation_steps: Coniferous trees (like pines) often live in cold climates. Their needle-like shape and waxy coating allow snow to slide off easily, preventing heavy snow accumulation that could break the branches.

questions.stem: A vaccine produces its effects by

options.A: directly attacking the antigens and neutralizing them.
options.B: coating the pathogens to increase their susceptibility by phagocytes.

explanation_steps: Vaccines introduce a weakened or dead pathogen into the body to trigger a primary immune response. This creates memory cells that allow the body to fight the real pathogen faster in the future.

questions.stem: A strategy that would **not** help restore a high body temperature to normal is

options.B: decrease in blood flow to the skin periphery.

explanation_steps: Shivering is a mechanism used to *increase* body temperature when it's too cold by generating heat through muscle friction. If the body is already hot, shivering would worsen the condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following respiratory organs is divided into the right and left bronchi?
explanation_steps: The trachea (windpipe) descends into the chest and bifurcates (splits) into two tubes called the right and left primary bronchi, which enter the lungs.

questions.stem: Receptors in the skin **cannot** sense
explanation_steps: Skin receptors (thermoreceptors, mechanoreceptors) sense heat, texture (touch), and vibration. Chemicals in the air are sensed by chemoreceptors in the nose (smell) and mouth (taste).

questions.stem: During food digestion, one of the end products of pancreatic juice is
explanation_steps: Pancreatic juice contains enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin, which break down proteins into peptides and eventually into amino acids (which are the end products).

questions.stem: All, except one, are the functions of plasma constituents.

options.A: Transport of nutrients, gases and vitamins

explanation_steps: All the options listed are functions of the different components of plasma. Plasma proteins include globulins (fight disease), fibrinogen (clotting), and albumin (pH/osmotic balance). It also transports nutrients and gases.

questions.stem: One of the following is **incorrect** of the thymus gland.

options.B: It is located behind the sternum.
options.D: It attains maximum size during adult age.

explanation_steps: The thymus gland is largest and most active during childhood/infancy. After puberty, it starts to shrink (involution) and is replaced by fat in adults. Therefore, it does NOT reach maximum size during adult age.

questions.stem: "Birds feed upon the insects disturbed by the feeding cattle". This symbiotic relationship is best described by
explanation_steps: This is a classic example of commensalism. The birds benefit by getting easy access to food (insects), while the cattle are neither helped nor harmed by the birds' presence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of dating an old fossil?
explanation_steps: Carbon-14 dating (radiocarbon dating) is the standard method used to determine the age of organic materials and fossils by measuring the decay of the radioactive carbon-14 isotope.

questions.stem: Which one is most probably **not** a source of genetic variation for evolution?
explanation_steps: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent producing offspring that are genetically identical (clones). This process provides very little to no genetic variation compared to sexual reproduction, mutation, or migration.

questions.stem: Which of the following ecological levels include the study of biogeochemical cycling through the environment?
explanation_steps: Ecosystem ecology studies the interactions between living organisms (biotic) and their physical environment (abiotic), which includes the movement of energy and the cycling of chemicals (biogeochemical cycles like carbon or nitrogen cycles).

questions.stem: Which statement **is not** true about the human heart?

options.A: The two upper chambers are called atria.
options.B: Relative to atria, ventricles have thick muscular walls.
options.C: The left side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs.
options.D: It is located in the thoracic cavity between the lungs.
options.E: Left ventricle has thicker walls than right ventricle.

explanation_steps: Statement C is false because the **right** side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The **left** side pumps oxygenated blood to the rest of the body (systemic circulation).

questions.stem: A bond that holds two complementary DNA strands is
explanation_steps: The two strands of the DNA double helix are held together by hydrogen bonds between the nitrogenous bases (Adenine-Thymine and Cytosine-Guanine). Covalent bonds (phosphodiester) hold the backbone of a single strand.

questions.stem: A germinating seed **does not** require
explanation_steps: During early germination, the seed uses its stored energy (in the endosperm or cotyledons). It does not need an external source of food (nutrients from soil) until it grows leaves and begins photosynthesis. Option C is also incorrect because germination usually requires oxygen (a

questions.stem: Ringworm disease is caused by
explanation_steps: Despite the name, ringworm is not caused by a worm. It is a fungal infection of the skin caused by a group of fungi called dermatophytes.

questions.stem: One of the following groups of organisms periodically shed their exoskeleton.
explanation_steps: Arthropods (like insects, spiders, and crabs) have a hard external skeleton made of chitin. Because this shell doesn't grow with them, they must periodically shed it and grow a new one in a process called molting or ecdysis.

questions.stem: During the process of transcription, a strand of ________ serves as a template.
explanation_steps: Transcription is the process where the genetic information in a specific segment of DNA is copied into a complementary strand of RNA (mRNA). Thus, DNA serves as the template.

questions.stem: Earthworms are **not**
explanation_steps: Earthworms are segmented annelids that live freely in the soil. They are scavengers that eat decaying organic matter, which aerates the soil and provides nutrients, making them 'farmer friendly'. They do not cause disease in plants, so they are not plant pathogens.

questions.stem: Which one of the following **is not** true of proteins?

options.A: They can be stored in the human body.
options.B: If in excess, they can be converted into carbohydrate.
options.D: Can be broken down to release energy.

explanation_steps: Unlike fats (stored in adipose tissue) or carbohydrates (stored as glycogen), the human body does not have a specialized storage system for proteins or amino acids. Excess protein is processed and converted into energy or other molecules (like carbohydrates/fats), but they aren't

questions.stem: When a hydrocarbon is burned in excess air,

options.A: energy is absorbed from the surrounding.
options.B: one compound and an element are produced.
options.C: both the substances formed have fixed volume.
options.D: carbon dioxide and water are produced.

explanation_steps: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon (like methane or propane) in the presence of sufficient oxygen (excess air) always produces carbon dioxide ($$ CO_2 $$) and water ($$ H_2O $$) while releasing energy (exothermic).

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is readily soluble in cyclohexane?
explanation_steps: Cyclohexane is a non-polar solvent. According to the 'like dissolves like' rule, non-polar solutes dissolve in non-polar solvents. Paraffin oil is non-polar, whereas water, ammonia, acetic acid, and alcohol are all polar.

questions.stem: The atomic number of Neon is 10. Then the electron configuration $$ [Ne]3s^23p^3 $$ represents the element
explanation_steps: To find the element, calculate the total number of electrons: Neon core (10) + 2 (from $$ 3s^2 $$) + 3 (from $$ 3p^3 $$) = 15. The element with atomic number 15 is Phosphorus (P).

questions.stem: One of the following is a decomposition product of $$ KClO_3 $$?
explanation_steps: When potassium chlorate ($$ KClO_3 $$) decomposes (usually with heat and a catalyst), it breaks down into potassium chloride ($$ KCl $$) and oxygen gas ($$ O_2 $$). $$ 2KClO_3 \rightarrow 2KCl + 3O_2 $$.

questions.stem: One of the following **is not** a constituent of a nucleic acid molecule.
explanation_steps: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorous (found in the phosphate group). Sulphur is a characteristic component of many proteins but is absent in nucleic acids.

questions.stem: If a doctor injects a patient with a solution and several red blood cells rupture, the injected solution is probably a
explanation_steps: Rupturing (hemolysis) occurs in a hypotonic solution. In such a solution, the concentration of solutes outside the cell is lower than inside, causing water to enter the cell by osmosis until it swells and bursts.

questions.stem: All of the following are plant hormones, except
explanation_steps: Auxins, cytokinins, and ethylene are major plant hormones (phytohormones). Glucagon is a hormone produced by the human pancreas to raise blood glucose levels.

questions.stem: The branch of chemistry that deals with the pollution of air, soil and water sources is
explanation_steps: Environmental chemistry is the scientific study of chemical phenomena in natural places, specifically focusing on how chemicals interact with the environment and the sources/effects of pollution.

questions.stem: The two processes involved in a simple distillation are
explanation_steps: Simple distillation is used to separate a solvent from a solution. It involves two phase changes: first, the liquid is heated to its boiling point to turn into gas (**evaporation**), and then the gas is cooled in a condenser to turn back into a liquid (**condensation**).

questions.stem: Two water molecules are held together by
explanation_steps: While the atoms *within* a water molecule are held by covalent bonds, the attraction *between* separate water molecules is due to **hydrogen bonding**. This occurs because the partially positive hydrogen of one molecule is attracted to the partially negative oxygen of another.

questions.stem: The bond angle in a molecule with a trigonal planar geometry is
explanation_steps: In a trigonal planar arrangement (like in $$ BF_3 $$ or $$ CO_3^{2-} $$), three electron groups are spread as far apart as possible around a central atom in a flat plane. This creates an angle of exactly $$ 120^\circ $$ ($$ 360/3 $$).

questions.stem: When a piece of reactive metal is dropped into hydrochloric acid, the gas evolved,

options.C: is the lightest of all gases.
options.D: pollutes the air when it burns.

explanation_steps: The reaction between a metal and acid produces a salt and **hydrogen gas** ($$ H_2 $$). Hydrogen is the lightest gas in the universe (Choice C) and is highly flammable, burning with a 'pop' sound (Choice B). Since both are true, E is the answer.

questions.stem: Ammonium nitrate can be best used as
explanation_steps: Ammonium nitrate ($$ NH_4NO_3 $$) is a high-nitrogen compound. It is primarily used in agriculture as a high-nutrient **fertilizer** because it provides nitrogen in two forms (ammonium and nitrate) that plants can easily absorb.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals **cannot** occur in a free state in the earth crust?
explanation_steps: Highly reactive metals like **sodium** react instantly with moisture and oxygen in the environment. Therefore, they are always found as compounds (like $$ NaCl $$) and never in a pure 'free' state. Gold, Silver, and Platinum are unreactive and can be found as pure nuggets.

questions.stem: When sodium carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid, the sum of the coefficients of all the reactants and products is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Write the balanced equation.**
$$ 1Na_2CO_3 + 2HCl 
ightarrow 2NaCl + 1H_2O + 1CO_2 $$
**Step 2: Sum the coefficients.**
Reactants: $$ 1 + 2 = 3 $$
Products: $$ 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 $$
Total Sum: $$ 3 + 4 = 7 $$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a natural polymer?
explanation_steps: Proteins, carbohydrates (like starch), natural rubber, and gums are polymers produced by living organisms. **Polythene** (polyethylene) is a synthetic polymer manufactured from ethylene in industrial processes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an endothermic process?
explanation_steps: **Evaporation** (changing from liquid to gas) requires the absorption of heat energy from the surroundings to break intermolecular forces. Processes that absorb heat are called **endothermic**. Combustion, condensation, and neutralization are typically exothermic (release heat).

questions.stem: Which of the following **is correct** about beta decay?

options.C: Beta particles are high speed protons
options.D: The atomic mass will not change

explanation_steps: In beta minus ($$ eta^- $$) decay, a neutron turns into a proton and an electron (the beta particle). The **atomic mass number (nucleon number) remains the same**, while the atomic number increases by 1. Choice D is correct because the overall mass number does not change.

explanation_steps:

$$ (1 \times 12) + (2 \times 1) + (1 \times 16) = 30 \text{ u} $$.
**Step 2:** Find the ratio ($$ n $$) of molecular mass to empirical mass.
$$ n = 180 / 30 = 6 $$.

questions.stem: Which element is associated with the term "galvanized"?
explanation_steps: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective coating of **Zinc** to steel or iron to prevent rusting.

questions.stem: The elements that have an outer electron configuration $$ ns^2 $$ are called
explanation_steps: Group 2 elements have two valence electrons in their outermost 's' orbital ($$ ns^2 $$). These elements are known as **alkaline earth metals** (e.g., Magnesium, Calcium).

questions.stem: If some amount of sodium chloride is dissolved in water, which of the following properties **is greater** for the salt solution compared to water?
explanation_steps: Adding a non-volatile solute like salt to water causes **boiling point elevation**. This means the salt solution will have a higher boiling point than pure water. (Note: Osmotic pressure also increases, but boiling point elevation is the primary physical property taught in this c

questions.stem:
The percentage composition of carbon in $$ CaCO_3 $$ is
**[At. Mass: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]**
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Find total molar mass of $$ CaCO_3 $$.
$$ 40 + 12 + (3 \times 16) = 100 \text{ g/mol} $$.
**Step 2:** Find % of carbon.
$$ (\text{Mass of C} / \text{Total mass}) \times 100 $$
$$ (12 / 100) \times 100 = 12\% $$.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements **is not** correct about carbon?

options.A: It occurs in a free as well as combined state.
options.C: Coke is an amorphous form of carbon.
options.D: It reduces hot concentrated nitric acid to nitrogen monoxide.
options.E: It cannot be used for jewelry.

explanation_steps: Diamond is an allotrope of carbon and is famously used in jewelry. Therefore, the statement saying it 'cannot be used for jewelry' is incorrect.

questions.stem: As water solidifies it does one of the following.
explanation_steps: Freezing (solidification) is an **exothermic** process, meaning it gives off heat. Uniquely, water **expands** when it turns into ice because of its hydrogen-bonded crystalline structure, making ice less dense than liquid water.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a polar molecule?
explanation_steps: Ammonia ($$ NH_3 $$) has a trigonal pyramidal shape with a lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen, creating an uneven distribution of charge. $$ O_2, N_2, $$ and $$ Cl_2 $$ are non-polar elements. $$ CO_2 $$ is linear and symmetrical, making it non-polar.

questions.stem: It is believed that carbon-14 in nature is slowly generated by the action of
explanation_steps:
Carbon-14 is produced in the upper atmosphere when cosmic ray-generated **neutrons** collide with **Nitrogen-14** atoms. The reaction is: $$ ^{14}_{7}N + ^{1}_{0}n 
ightarrow ^{14}_{6}C + ^{1}_{1}p $$.

questions.stem:
The total number of electrons in the M and N shells of Xenon respectively are
**[At. Number of Xe = 54]**
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Write the electron configuration for Xe (54).
$$ 1s^2, 2s^2 2p^6, 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10}, 4s^2 4p^6 4d^{10}, 5s^2 5p^6 $$.
**Step 2:** Identify shell counts.
- M shell (n=3): $$ 3s + 3p + 3d = 2 + 6 + 10 = 18 $$.
- N shell (n=4): $$ 4s + 4p + 4d = 2 + 6 + 10 = 18 $$.

questions.stem: When vinegar and baking soda are mixed together, ________ gas is formed?
explanation_steps: Vinegar is acetic acid and baking soda is sodium bicarbonate. Their reaction produces sodium acetate, water, and **carbon dioxide** gas, which causes the mixture to foam and bubble.

questions.stem:
In molecular oxygen ($$ O_2 $$), the number of unshared electron pairs on each oxygen atom is
**[At. Number of O = 8]**
explanation_steps: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons. In $$ O_2 $$, two oxygen atoms share two pairs of electrons to form a double bond ($$ O=O $$). This leaves 4 valence electrons on each atom, arranged into **2 unshared pairs** (lone pairs).

questions.stem: Which of the following technologies is **not** utilized for power generation today?
explanation_steps: **Nuclear fusion** is the process that powers the sun, but scientists have not yet succeeded in making it a commercially viable or utilized source for general power grids. Nuclear fission (D) is widely used in current nuclear power plants.

questions.stem: The enthalpy change involved when one mole of a compound is formed from its constituent elements is called heat of
explanation_steps: The standard enthalpy of **formation** ($$ \Delta H_f $$) is the energy change that occurs when exactly one mole of a substance is formed from its pure elements in their standard states.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds **is not** an electrolyte when dissolved in water?
explanation_steps: Electrolytes are substances that ionize in water to conduct electricity (salts, strong acids, and bases). **Methanol ($$ CH_3OH $$)** is a covalent molecular compound (an alcohol) that dissolves but does not form ions, making it a non-electrolyte.

questions.stem: 2-Methyl-3-hexanone is an example of
explanation_steps: The suffix **'-one'** in the IUPAC name indicates that the functional group is a carbonyl group ($$ C=O $$) located within the carbon chain, which defines a **ketone**.

questions.stem: The salt bridge in an electrochemical cell

options.C: serves as a simple mechanical bridge.

explanation_steps: A salt bridge contains an electrolyte solution. Its primary purpose is to **allow ions to migrate** between the two half-cells to maintain electrical neutrality. Electrons flow through the external wire, not the salt bridge.

questions.stem: What type of proportionality exists between the solubility of a gas in a liquid and the liquid temperature?
explanation_steps: Generally, the solubility of gases in liquids **decreases** as the temperature **increases**. This is an **inverse** relationship. (This is why warm soda loses its fizz faster than cold soda).

questions.stem: An object is moving in circular motion covering half of the circumference. If the radius of the circle is 12 m, the magnitude of the displacement of the object is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Understand displacement. Displacement is the straight-line distance between the starting point and the ending point.
**Step 2:** In half a circle, the object moves from one side to the exact opposite side.
**Step 3:** The straight line connecting these two points is t

questions.stem: The number of significant figures in 0.00570 is
explanation_steps:
According to the rules of significant figures:
1. Leading zeros (0.00...) are **never** significant.
2. Non-zero digits (5, 7) are **always** significant.
3. Trailing zeros in a decimal number (...70) **are** significant.
Thus, 5, 7, and the final 0 are significant (3 figures).

questions.stem: The speed of a body in a certain direction is
explanation_steps: Velocity is defined as speed with a specified direction. It is a vector quantity, unlike speed, which is a scalar quantity and does not include direction.

explanation_steps:

questions.stem: Materials that recover their original shape and size when the force is removed after they are stretched, compressed, bent or twisted are
explanation_steps: Elasticity is the property of a material that allows it to return to its original shape and size once the deforming forces are removed. Examples include rubber bands and springs.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards into the air from a handball player's hand. It reached a maximum height of 20 m. It stopped momentarily and falls back to the handball player's hand. The total distance and total displacement travelled by the ball respectively, are
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Total distance is the sum of every step. Upward ($$ 20\text{ m} $$) + Downward ($$ 20\text{ m} $$) = $$ 40\text{ m} $$.
**Step 2:** Displacement is the difference between final and initial positions. Since it returned to the hand, the net change is $$ 0 $$.

questions.stem: A thermometer that combines the maximum and minimum thermometers consisting of U-shaped glass tube is
explanation_steps: Six's thermometer (also known as a Maximum-Minimum thermometer) uses a U-shaped tube with mercury and alcohol to simultaneously record the highest and lowest temperatures reached during a period (e.g., 24 hours).

explanation_steps:

explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** The cyclist's velocity ($$ V_c $$) is 40 km/h South. The wind's velocity ($$ V_w $$) is 30 km/h West.
**Step 2:** Velocity relative to wind ($$ V_{cw} $$) is the vector subtraction: $$ \vec{V}_{cw} = \vec{V}_c - \vec{V}_w $$.

questions.stem: An electric bulb works on 220 V source supply and draws a current of 0.4 A. The power of the electric bulb, in watts, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Identify given values: Voltage ($$ V $$) = 220 V, Current ($$ I $$) = 0.4 A.
**Step 2:** Use the electric power formula: $$ P = V \times I $$.
**Step 3:** $$ P = 220 \times 0.4 = 88 \text{ Watts} $$.

questions.stem: We see the image of our face when we look into a mirror. This is due to ________ of light.
explanation_steps: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it hits a surface. Mirrors have smooth, polished surfaces that reflect light rays in a predictable way, allowing us to see images.

questions.stem: The quantity of heat needed to change one kilogram of a substance from its solid to liquid state at its melting point is
explanation_steps: Latent heat of fusion is the energy required to change a substance from solid to liquid (or vice versa) without a change in temperature. Latent heat of vaporization refers to liquid-to-gas change.

questions.stem: The human eye forms the image of an object at its
explanation_steps: The retina is the light-sensitive inner lining of the eye. It acts like the film in a camera or the sensor in a digital camera, where the lens focuses the light to form an inverted image.

questions.stem: The value of magnetic field that causes a maximum force of $$ 7 \times 10^{-3} \text{ N} $$ on a 20 cm wire carrying current of 10 A will be
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Identify given values: Force ($$ F $$) = $$ 7 \times 10^{-3} \text{ N} $$, Current ($$ I $$) = 10 A, Length ($$ L $$) = 20 cm = 0.2 m.
**Step 2:** Maximum force occurs when the wire is perpendicular ($$ \sin 90^\circ = 1 $$). Formula: $$ F = B \\times I \\times L $

questions.stem: When light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it tends to

options.A: speed up and bend away from the normal.
options.B: speed up and bend towards the normal.
options.C: slow down and bend away from the normal.
options.D: slow down and bend towards the normal.

explanation_steps: Light slows down when moving into a denser medium (higher refractive index). This decrease in speed causes the light ray to bend towards the normal line.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** true of pressure in liquids?

options.D: Pressure depends on the density of the liquid.
options.E: Pressure does not depend on the shape of the container.

explanation_steps: Pressure in a static liquid acts equally in all directions (sideways, upwards, downwards) at any given depth. It is not limited to only acting downwards.

questions.stem: Decibel is the unit used for
explanation_steps: The decibel (dB) is a logarithmic unit used to express the ratio of two values of a physical quantity, commonly used to measure the intensity level (loudness level) of sound.

questions.stem: The relative density of mercury is 13.6. Its density, in kg/m$$^3$$, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Relative density is the ratio of a substance's density to the density of water.
**Step 2:** Density of water is $$ 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3 $$.
**Step 3:** Density = Relative Density $$ \times $$ Density of Water.
**Step 4:** $$ 13.6 \\times 1000 = 13600 \\text{ kg/m}^3

questions.stem: Which of the following is suitable for making permanent magnet?
explanation_steps: Steel is a 'hard' magnetic material. While it is difficult to magnetize, it retains its magnetism for a long time, making it suitable for permanent magnets. Soft iron is used for temporary magnets (electromagnets).

questions.stem: A block of metal weighs 6 N in air and 4 N when immersed in a liquid. The buoyant force on the block is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Buoyant force (upthrust) is the loss in weight of an object when immersed in a fluid.
**Step 2:** $$ F_{buoyant} = \text{Weight in Air} - \text{Weight in Liquid} $$.
**Step 3:** $$ F_{buoyant} = 6 \text{ N} - 4 \text{ N} = 2 \text{ N} $$.

questions.stem: A step up transformer converts ________ into ________

options.A: low voltage at low current, high voltage at high current
options.B: high voltage at low current, low voltage at high current
options.C: low voltage at high current, high voltage at low current
options.D: high voltage at high current, low voltage at low current

explanation_steps: A step-up transformer increases voltage. Because energy is conserved ($$ P = VI $$), as voltage increases, current must decrease. Thus, it converts low voltage (high current) to high voltage (low current).

questions.stem: Speed of sound is maximum in
explanation_steps: Sound is a mechanical wave that travels through the vibration of particles. In solids, particles are packed tightly together, allowing the vibration to transfer much faster than in liquids or gases. Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** correct about sound and light?

options.A: Sound waves are mechanical waves whereas light waves are electromagnetic waves.
options.B: Sound waves cannot travel through vacuum whereas light waves can travel through vacuum.
options.C: Sound waves are longitudinal waves whereas light waves are transverse waves.
options.D: Velocity of light depends on temperature whereas velocity of sound is independent of temperature.
options.E: The speed of sound is much less than the speed of light in air.

explanation_steps: Statement D is incorrect because the velocity of **sound** depends heavily on temperature (it increases as air gets warmer), whereas the speed of **light** is generally considered constant in a given medium regardless of temperature.

questions.stem: A spectral line is created by the movement between allowed energy levels of a(n)
explanation_steps: Spectral lines are produced when an **electron** jumps from one energy level (orbital) to another. When it moves to a lower level, it emits a photon of specific wavelength, creating an emission line.

questions.stem: In the experimental study of photoelectric effect, the photoelectric current is

options.A: inversely proportional to the number of photoelectrons emitted per second.
options.B: inversely proportional to the intensity of radiation.
options.C: directly proportional to the frequency of the incident radiation.
options.D: directly proportional to the intensity of radiation.
options.E: directly proportional to the work function of the metal.

explanation_steps: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the **intensity** of the light (keeping frequency constant) increases the number of photons hitting the surface, which increases the number of emitted electrons, and thus increases the **photoelectric current**.

questions.stem: Majority of the mass of an atom is concentrated on
explanation_steps: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, which are nearly 2000 times heavier than electrons. Thus, over 99.9% of an atom's mass is concentrated in the tiny central nucleus discovered by Rutherford.
